case_title: State through Deputy Superintendent of Police v. R. Soundirarasu etc.
accused_occupation: Motor Vehicle Inspector (Grade 1), a public servant (Respondent No. 1); Respondent No. 2 is described as a commerce graduate claiming independent income
accused_socioeconomic_status: Alleged in the FIR only: accused described as hailing from an ordinary agricultural family. The Court made no finding on wealth or class.
statutory_provisions: Prevention of Corruption Act 1988 s.13(2) r/w s.13(1)(e); Indian Penal Code s.109 (abetment)
evidence_type: Documentary: FIR, asset, income and expenditure statements in the charge sheet, income tax returns, and the accused's written explanation. No trial evidence had been recorded.
trial_court_outcome: Special Judge rejected both discharge applications under s.239 CrPC (orders dated 29.03.2016); no sentence, as the case was at the charge stage
high_court_outcome: Revision allowed; orders rejecting discharge set aside; both accused discharged from the charges
neutral_facts: A public servant working as a motor vehicle inspector in a regional transport office was alleged to have acquired and possessed assets disproportionate to his known sources of income during a check period from 1 January 2002 to 31 March 2004. The allegation was that assets were held in the names of the accused's spouse, the accused's father-in-law and the accused's minor son, and that these were in substance held by the accused. Information was received and a preliminary verification was made, after which a First Information Report was registered in September 2005. The complaint listed house sites, lands, a house construction, gold and silver ornaments and household articles, and stated that the family's expenditure exceeded the recorded income for the period. During the investigation, the investigating officer called for an explanation from the accused, who replied in November 2007 denying that he held disproportionate assets. He also furnished income tax returns filed by the spouse from 1990 onwards and returns of a partnership firm from 1993. The investigation found that the spouse had no sufficient independent source of income to acquire the assets, and the spouse was identified as an abettor. The investigating agency then filed a charge sheet.
attempt_completion: Completed (as alleged: possession of disproportionate assets)
number_of_offences: 3 charged (PC Act s.13(2), s.13(1)(e), IPC s.109); 0 finally upheld
financial_property_loss: Alleged disproportionate assets of Rs. 24,41,980 (prosecution figure; not a finding)
key_evidence_accepted: Charge-sheet material and documents on record, considered prima facie. The Court relied on them to hold the charge was not groundless; it made no finding on the truth of the explanations.
post_offence_conduct: Accused gave a written explanation to the investigating officer on 1.11.2007 denying disproportionate assets; the Court did not decide its merits.
trial_duration: offence: check period 01.01.2002 to 31.03.2004 (FIR dated 19.09.2005); trial judgment: 29.03.2016; High Court: 27.04.2017; Supreme Court: 05.09.2022
legal_representation: For the State (appellant): V. Krishnamurthy, AAG, with others. For the accused (respondents): K. Radhakrishnan, Sr. Adv., with others.
investigation_status: FIR registered 19.09.2005; investigation concluded; charge sheet filed as Special Criminal Case No. 36/2008; charges not yet framed
appeal_history: Trial court (Special Judge): discharge rejected 29.03.2016. High Court: revision allowed 27.04.2017, accused discharged. Supreme Court: State's appeals allowed, discharge orders set aside, charges to be framed.
prosecution_argument: The High Court wrongly applied a beyond-reasonable-doubt standard at the s.239 stage, considered defence documents and conducted a mini trial, and misapplied Suresh Rajan and Debendra Nath Padhi.
defence_argument: Wife was an independent income earner and income tax assessee, so her assets should not be attributed to the accused; the explanation was not considered; the accused needed only to show a preponderance of probability.
legal_principle_applied: At s.239 the court only asks whether the charge is groundless; s.13(1)(e) shifts the onus of explanation to the accused, but it cannot be discharged at discharge stage. Revisional power is limited to correcting manifest error of law or procedure.
precedent_relied_upon: State of Maharashtra v. Wasudeo Ramchandra Kaidalwar (1981) 3 SCC 199; Central Bureau of Investigation v. T.H. Vijayalakshmi (2021 SCC OnLine SC 923); Onkar Nath Mishra v. State (NCT of Delhi) (2008) 2 SCC 561; State of T.N. v. N. Suresh Rajan (2014) 11 SCC 709; K. Veeraswami v. Union of India (1991) 3 SCC 655; Munna Devi v. State of Rajasthan (2001) 9 SCC 631
other_sentence_order: Special Court directed to frame charges and try the accused; the Court's observations are not final on guilt or innocence

appeal_history.quote: The High Court has completely ignored that it was not at the stage of trial or considering an appeal against a verdict in a trial.

prosecution_argument.quote: the High Court has erroneously cast a burden on the prosecution to prove the case against the accused persons beyond all reasonable doubt even at the stage of framing charge.
